newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 20.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 20. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The new director of the Indonesian Atomic Energy Authority (Batan) said construction of the country's first controversial nuclear power plant on the island of Java is set to begin if the plan gets government approval.
State Minister for Development Planning Ginandjar Kartasasmita warned of the danger of Indonesian non-governmental organisations acting as fronts for foreign political interests in the country.

President Suharto said that individual holdings of companies listed on the Jakarta Stock Exchange should not exceed 15 percent as this was approaching a monopoly. It was not clear whether Suharto's comments refered to recent trading in the country's largest automobile manufacturer PT Astra Internasional.

East Timorese Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo has denied making remarks in German magazine 'Der Spiegel' that caused a recent stir in Indonesia, according to armed forces (ABRI) chief General Feisal Tanjung. Anti-Belo protests broke out in Jakarta last week after it was reported that Belo had said Indonesia treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs."
